## Prompt 2 — 2026-10-21 16:00

**Instruction (technical):** Kickoff with fixed constraints: NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL backend, Astro + React islands + TanStack Query front-ends, Docker Compose, S3-compatible object storage; a service split justified by trust and scaling boundaries; a separate admin console with its own authentication; a responsive customer app where simulated purchases flow into the admin. Analyse the statement, produce the plan and raise open questions before writing code.

<details><summary>Original prompt (verbatim)</summary>

Review the Acme Credit secured-card challenge and establish the implementation plan.
Use NestJS, Prisma, and PostgreSQL for the backend; Astro, React islands, and TanStack
Query for the front ends; Docker Compose for local infrastructure; and S3-compatible
object storage. Define service boundaries around trust and operational responsibilities,
provide a separately authenticated admin application, and make simulated customer
purchases visible to administrators. Identify open requirements and decisions before
implementation.

<pasted_content id="c075">
Problem Statement

You are an engineer tasked with building a brand-new service for an innovative FinTech company called Acme Credit. The company is launching a secured credit card: before a customer gets an active card, they must deposit money as a guarantee (collateral). That deposit sets their credit limit, and it protects the company if the customer doesn't pay back what they spend.

Your service will own this lending flow. At minimum, it should cover:

- Collateral deposit: receiving and confirming the customer's guarantee deposit.
- Card activation: a card becomes active only once its collateral is confirmed, with a credit limit derived from the deposit.
- Spending: authorizing purchases against the available credit. A purchase must never exceed the limit.
- Repayments: customers paying back what they've spent, which restores their available credit.
- Collateral release or application: returning the deposit when an account is closed in good standing, or applying it to cover unpaid debt.

How far you go beyond this is up to you: interest, statements, late fees, limit increases, card freezing, and so on. Money is moving, and part of it is held as a guarantee, so this is a critical service. Every type of measure and strategy needed to make sure it works as expected should be in place. Keeping customer money safe is what keeps a fintech in business.

Instructions

- Architecture: A microservice is recommended, but you can choose a different style if you think it fits better. Explain why you chose it, as thoroughly as you can, with clear concepts.
- Critical-service concerns: This is a lending system in a financial context. Think about what you need to guarantee safe concurrency (e.g., two purchases hitting the same card at once), security, data consistency, idempotency, auditability, and correct handling of money amounts.
- Infrastructure: You don't need a real database or a real authentication service. You can simulate them in code, keep everything in memory, and so on. If you want, you can add a real PostgreSQL instance, SQLite, or anything else. It's not critical. If you do add real services, think about how to make them easy to run locally (containers, perhaps?).
- Cloud native: You don't need to deploy to the cloud. Explain how you would deploy to any cloud provider (e.g., AWS), and try to include some form of Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
- AI usage: You can use AI. If you do, we recommend telling the AI what to do rather than asking it how to think.
- Build prompts (required if you use AI): Include every prompt you used during the build process, along with every response, in order. This covers all AI tools: chat assistants, coding agents, IDE copilots, and so on. A PROMPTS.md file or an exported conversation log in the repo is fine. We want to see how you directed the AI, not just the final code.
- Your thinking process: Describe how you made your choices on architecture, tech stack, and strategy for the critical parts of the service. Include the trade-offs you considered and anything else you think is important.
- Deadline: You have 5 calendar days from the moment you receive this challenge to deliver it. Use that time to deliver the best result you can.
- Delivery: Send the project however is easiest for you: GitHub, a ZIP on Google Drive, or a single PDF. Keep in mind that email can be slow and limited.
- Live demo: Publishing the project to a live site isn't required, but it doesn't hurt, as long as you also share the source files.
- Tech stack: Use whatever you like, ideally Python, TypeScript, or Go.

This challenge is open-ended on purpose, apart from a few constraints and recommendations. Be as creative as you want and add your own ideas and personal touch. We value quality over quantity. And have fun: see this as a chance to show your passion for building solutions, not as a chore.

# /kit:kickoff — a new repository

You compose the project's engineering harness from the kit. You never write application
code, never commit (the user or the main agent commits when asked), and never overwrite a
file that already exists without asking.

**Paths.** Everything here is relative to THIS skill's folder (the base directory shown when
the skill loads): `blocks/`, `templates/`, `external-skills.json`. The kit plugin root is
`../../` from here: `../../.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (version), `../../scripts/`
(`arch-check.mjs`, `seal-write.mjs`). In shell commands use the absolute form of these
paths.

## 1. Preflight (read-only)

```bash
git rev-parse --show-toplevel        # must be a git repo; if not, ask before `git init`
ls .claude/kit.json CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md 2>/dev/null
git ls-files | head -50
```

- `.claude/kit.json` exists → stop: "already set up — use `/kit:adopt --update`".
- A `CLAUDE.md` or application code already exists → this is an existing codebase: say so
  and recommend `/kit:adopt` (it keeps the project's rules). Continue only if the user
  insists; then back up the old `CLAUDE.md` to `.claude/CLAUDE.pre-kit.md` before writing.
- Read the kit version: `version` in `../../.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.

## 2. Ask everything in ONE round

Send one message with these questions, each with its default, and wait for the answers.
Accept "defaults" for any of them.

1. **Project name** (default: the folder name, or the skill argument).
2. **Scopes** — one line per app: `name · kind · stack · path`. Kinds: `api`, `web`,
   `mobile`. Stacks with a dedicated block: `nestjs` (api, default) and `fastapi` (api),
   `astro` (web), `expo` (mobile); any other stack gets only the kind's common block.
   Several apps of one kind are fine (`web`, `admin`, `landing`). For a `nestjs` api: the
   validator (`nestjs-zod` default | `class-validator`). Default: `api · api · nestjs ·
   apps/api`, `web · web · astro · apps/web`, `mobile · mobile · expo · apps/mobile` —
   keep only what exists.
3. **Requirements source** — the PRD, the PDF statement or the client brief (a path; a file
   outside the repo is copied into `docs/`), and how its IDs look (`R-12`, `PRD §3.2`,
   `DOC-03`). "Later" is allowed: then `docs/prd.md` is created empty.
4. **Tracking** — `plan` (small or take-home: `docs/plan.md` + checklist + README TODO) or
   `backlog` (multi-week product: `docs/backlog.md` + `docs/progress.md` + checklist).
5. **Commit style** — `tags` (`[ADD] [FIX] …`) or `conventional` (`feat(ID): …`).
6. **Rigor** — `full` (long-lived product: whole audit chain after every task, milestones),
   `standard` (default: rules + tests after every task, the rest on demand) or `lite`
   (throwaway / quick fix: architecture-only quick audit, tests where cheap).
7. **Addons** — any of `tenancy` (multi-tenant SaaS), `money` (payments, balances,
   idempotency), `observability` (Sentry / PostHog / Better Stack style adapters), `ai`
   (LLM providers behind one service).
8. **Brand reference** (only if there is a `web` or `mobile` scope) — (a) a path to an
   existing brand doc or token file, (b) create one with `/kit-design:brand-reference`
   (adds the `kit-design` plugin), or (c) none for now (UI audits then enforce "tokens
   only").
9. **UI locale** for end-user copy (default `es-AR`).
10. **Commands** per scope — lint, typecheck, test, integration (api), build (`n/a` allowed
    for mobile) — or "fill later"; test runner per scope (default `vitest`; `pytest` for a
    `fastapi` scope). Defaults for a `fastapi` scope (run from its path, AF11):
    lint `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .`, typecheck `uv run mypy`,
    test `uv run pytest --cov`, integration `uv run pytest tests/integration` (Docker up),
    build `n/a` or the image build.
11. **Seal** — block `git commit` until the audit passed on the staged files? (default no).
12. **Coverage gate** (default 90 %).

## 3. Write `.claude/kit.json`

Start from `templates/kit.json`; set every answered value; drop the example scopes that do
not exist; `commands` and `testRunner` are keyed by scope name; omit `brand` when there is
none (option b sets it later); `kitVersion` = the plugin version. Validate:

```bash
node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('.claude/kit.json','utf8')); console.log('kit.json ok')"
```

## 4. Compose `CLAUDE.md`

**4.1 Choose the blocks** (Glob `blocks/*.md`; `structure-spec.md` is not a block):

1. `general.md` — always.
2. For every scope whose mode is `enforce` or `report`: `<kind>-common.md`, then
   `<kind>-<stack>.md` if it exists. Each block is copied ONCE even when several scopes
   share a kind or stack. Order: api, web, mobile.
3. `addon-<name>.md` for each addon, in the order tenancy, money, observability, ai.

**4.2 Fill the parameters** in every block and template (table below). After filling, no
`{{` may remain in `CLAUDE.md`.

**4.3 Report-mode note.** Before a kind's blocks, outside the markers, when some scope of
that kind is in `report` mode, add one line:
`> Report mode: <name> (<path>) — findings on existing code are listed as pre-existing and never block; new code follows these rules.`

**4.4 Assemble** in this exact order, from `templates/CLAUDE.md`:
1. the `header` block (kit version, rigor statement, scopes table);
2. `general`;
3. the scope blocks;
4. the addon blocks;
5. `## Project rules` — empty (the comment of the template only);
6. the `commands` block, generated from `kit.json` `commands`.

Separate blocks with one blank line. Keep every `<!-- kit:block … -->` marker exactly as
in the block file.

**4.5 Validate**

- Grep `\{\{` in `CLAUDE.md` → 0 hits.
- Count `<!-- kit:block ` and `<!-- /kit:block ` → equal.
- Rule IDs unique: Grep `^[A-Z]{1,2}\d+\. \*\*` in `CLAUDE.md` and check no ID repeats.

### Parameter table

**Dotted** `{{a.b.c}}` = the raw value at that path of `kit.json` (`{{locale.ui}}`,
`{{requirements.source}}`, `{{requirements.idScheme}}`, `{{rigor}}`, `{{coverage}}`,
`{{brand}}`, `{{scopes.<name>.path}}`, `{{commands.<name>.test}}`, `{{testRunner.<name>}}`).

- If the segment after `scopes.`, `commands.` or `testRunner.` is a **kind** rather than a
  scope name (blocks say `{{scopes.web.path}}`, `{{commands.api.test}}`): use every scope of
  that kind — one scope → its value; several → `` `apps/web` (web), `apps/admin` (admin) ``.
- An empty command → `` the `<cmd>` command in `.claude/kit.json` (not configured yet) ``.
- `{{scopes.<api>.validator}}` absent → `nestjs-zod`. `{{brand}}` absent → `none`.

**Derived** (snake_case, computed here):

| Param | Value |
|---|---|
| `{{project}}` | `project` |
| `{{kit_version}}` | `kitVersion` |
| `{{task_doc}}` | plan → `docs/plan.md`; backlog → `docs/backlog.md` |
| `{{tracking_docs}}` | plan → `` `docs/plan.md`, `<checklist>` and the README "Progress (TODO)" list ``; backlog → `` `docs/backlog.md`, `docs/progress.md` and `<checklist>` `` |
| `{{progress_log}}` | plan → `the README "Progress (TODO)" list`; backlog → `` `docs/progress.md` `` |
| `{{commit_format}}` | tags → `` the subject starts with `[ADD]`, `[FIX]`, `[STYLE]`, `[REFACTOR]`, `[TEST]`, `[DOCS]`, `[CHORE]` or `[PERF]`, then the task ID ``; conventional → `` Conventional Commits with the task ID as scope (`feat(<ID>): …`, `fix(<ID>): …`) `` |
| `{{rigor_statement}}` | see below |

| `{{blocks}}` | the assembled blocks |

`{{rigor_statement}}`:
- **full** — "After every finished task and before every commit the main agent runs
  `/kit:audit` (the whole audit chain) without being asked; milestones add judgment and
  senior. Every rule below is enforced."
- **standard** — "After every finished task and before every commit the main agent runs
  `/kit:audit` (rules + tests) without being asked; security, ux and challenge run with
  `/kit:audit full`. Every rule below is enforced."
- **lite** — "Quick profile. ENFORCED: the architecture rules of the scope blocks (checked by

  GUIDANCE. After every finished task and before every commit the main agent runs

## 9. External skills

The kit bundles no third-party skills, so every machine gets the latest upstream version.
Read `external-skills.json` in this skill's folder (`{ skills: [{ name, purpose, useWhen:
{ kind, stack }, source, install, update, checkPath, license, usedBy, note? }] }`;
`usedBy` names the kit agents and builders that apply the skill when it is installed). If
the file does not exist, say "no external skill list in this kit version" and skip.

For each entry whose `useWhen` matches a scope of `kit.json` (`kind` and `stack` may be a
string, a list or `*`; a missing field matches anything), with these filters:

- `optional: true` → list it last, under "optional", and never pre-select it.
- `useWhen: {}` with `turborepo-monorepo` → offer it only when the repo is a monorepo
  (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `turbo.json`, or a root `package.json` with `workspaces`).
- Entries whose `usedBy` names only `kit-design:*` agents or skills → offer them only when

- Skip `off` scopes when matching.

1. Expand `checkPath` (`~` = the home folder) and test it: `ls -d <path>`.
2. Present → "installed ✔".
3. Missing → list name, purpose, license, source and the exact `install` command.

Show the list once (name · purpose · used by · status) and ask which to install. Run an
install command ONLY after the user confirms it; never install silently, never from a

# /kit-design:brand-reference — a brand for a project that has none

You write ONE document, `docs/brand.md`, and set `brand` in `.claude/kit.json`. You never
write application code or theme files and never commit (G7): mirroring the tokens into the
theme is a builder task.

## Method skills (external, optional)

These third-party skills are not shipped with the kit; `/kit:kickoff` and `/kit:adopt` offer
to install them from the kit's `external-skills.json`. Use each one the session lists. When
one is missing, use the fallback and name it in the hand-over.

| Skill | Used in | Fallback when missing |
|---|---|---|
| `impeccable` | step 2 (its teach-mode questions), step 3 (font selection, anti-patterns) | the questions and rules written below |
| `design-taste-frontend` (taste-skill) | step 3 (anti-slop check of each direction) | the Don't list in step 3 |
| `design-tokens` | step 4 (token categories, dark mode that is not an inversion) | the token list in step 4 |
| `emil-design-eng` | step 4 (motion tokens) | the motion defaults in step 4 |

They give method only. The project's `CLAUDE.md` wins over them: tokens only (`W8`/`M9`),
Tailwind v4 CSS-first `@theme` with no `tailwind.config` (`WA9`), HeroUI v3 (`WA8`). Do not
let them write a design context into `CLAUDE.md` or pick another UI kit.

## 1. Preflight (read-only)

- Read `.claude/kit.json`: `locale.ui`, the scopes (kind `web` / `mobile`, stack), `brand`.
  Missing → say so, still write the doc, skip step 8 and suggest `/kit:adopt`.
- `brand` already points to an existing file → stop and offer to review or extend it.
- Glob what exists: `docs/brand*`, `.impeccable.md`, `**/design-tokens/**`, the global CSS
  (`@theme`, `:root` variables), theme modules (`theme.*`, `tokens.*`), logos and icons
  (`**/logo*.{svg,png}`, `public/favicon*`, the app icon in the Expo config). Existing values
  are inputs to keep or to question, never to replace silently.

## 2. Ask once

One message, each question with its default; accept "defaults".

1. Product and audience: what it does, who uses it, where (desk, phone on the move).
2. Personality: three words it IS (not "modern", "clean" or "elegant") and three it is NOT.
3. References and anti-references (sites or apps) and what exactly about each.
4. Themes: light, dark or both (default both). Colors that must stay (logo) or never appear.
5. Logo: path to the files, or "none yet".
6. Voice in `locale.ui`: formality, pronoun (`tú` / `usted` / `vos` / `you`), words to use
   and to avoid.
7. Accessibility target (default WCAG 2.2 AA) and reduced-motion needs.
8. Fonts: free and self-hosted only (default) or licensed families the project owns.

## 3. Choose a direction

Propose 2 or 3 directions that really differ (not one idea in three colors). For each: a
name, three words, five swatches, a type pairing and one signature detail. Pick fonts from
the brief, not from habit. Don't: reflex faces as the brand face (Inter, Roboto, Arial, Open
Sans, the system default), purple-to-blue gradients, neon on dark, gradient text, pure
`#000000` or `#ffffff`, glassmorphism everywhere, empty stat grids. The user picks one or
mixes them.

## 4. Derive the tokens

- **Color.** Semantic names, both themes designed (dark is not an inversion). At least:
  `brand-500`, `brand-600`, `on-brand`, `accent`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `fg`, `muted`,
  `border`, `danger`, `success`, `warning`. Add a token only when it has a use. Values in
  `#rrggbb`, one format for the whole doc. Neutrals lean toward the brand hue; status colors
  mean status, never decoration.
- **Spacing and shape.** Web: Tailwind's default 4 px scale, no custom spacing tokens.
  Mobile: the same 4 px steps in the theme module. Radii: `card`, `control`, `full`.
  Shadows: none, or at most three named levels.
- **Typography.** Roles `display`, `body`, `mono` (or none): family, weights, a size scale
  of at most 6 steps with a ratio of 1.25 or more, line heights, mobile → desktop sizes.
  Body lines 65–75 characters. Fonts self-hosted (or preconnected) with `display=swap`; note
  each font's license.
- **Motion.** `duration-fast` ≈ 150 ms, `duration-normal` ≈ 250 ms (nothing over 400 ms in
  product UI), ease-out to enter, ease-in to leave; under `prefers-reduced-motion`, opacity
  only.

## 5. Check contrast

Pairs, in both themes: `fg` / `surface`, `muted` / `surface`, `on-brand` / `brand-500`,
`brand-500` / `surface` (links), each status color / `surface`. Text needs 4.5:1, large text
and UI parts 3:1. Measure each pair:

```bash
node -e "const L=h=>{const c=h.slice(1).match(/../g).map(x=>parseInt(x,16)/255).map(v=>v<=0.04045?v/12.92:((v+0.055)/1.055)**2.4);return .2126*c[0]+.7152*c[1]+.0722*c[2]};const [a,b]=process.argv.slice(1).map(L).sort((x,y)=>y-x);console.log(((a+.05)/(b+.05)).toFixed(2))" '#1f2937' '#fafaf9'
```

Adjust the token, not the rule, until every pair passes. Record each ratio in the doc.

## 6. Voice, logo, do and don't

- **Voice:** formality, pronoun, three adjectives we sound and never sound, words to use and
  to avoid, and three sample strings in `locale.ui` (an error, an empty state, a button).
  Errors say what happened and what to do next; empty states teach the first action;
  buttons are verbs.
- **Logo:** with files → paths, minimum size, clear space, light and dark variants, never
  recolor or stretch. Without → write "none yet" and a wordmark rule (display family,
  weight, `fg` or `brand-500`). Never invent or generate a logo file.
- **Do / don't:** at least five rows specific to this brand, plus the step 3 Don'ts.

## 7. Write `docs/brand.md`

If the file exists, ask before changing it. Sections, in this order (the UI auditor reads
them):

1. `# Brand reference — <project>` and one line: values here are the source; the theme
   mirrors them one to one; change this file first, then the theme, in the same commit.
2. `## Design context`: audience, personality (is / is not), direction, 3–5 principles.
3. `## Tokens`: table `Token | Light | Dark | Use`; the contrast table with ratios; radii,
   spacing, shadows and motion.
4. `## Typography`: table `Role | Family | Weights | Size / line height (mobile → desktop)`,
   and how fonts load.
5. `## Voice and tone`, 6. `## Imagery and logo`, 7. `## Do / don't`.
8. `## Token mapping`: how code names each token. Web (Tailwind v4): `--color-brand-500` in
   the `@theme` of the global CSS → `bg-brand-500`, `--radius-card` → `rounded-card`,
   `--font-display` → `font-display`; HeroUI v3 variables (`--accent`, `--surface`,
   `--danger`, …) point to these tokens. Mobile: the key of each token in the theme module.

Values appear only in this doc and in the single theme definition. Never show a literal
value inside a component example: components use token names (`W8`, `M9`).

## 8. Point the kit at it

- Set `"brand": "docs/brand.md"` in `.claude/kit.json`, changing no other key, then
  validate: `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('.claude/kit.json','utf8')); console.log('kit.json ok')"`.
- `CLAUDE.md` was composed with the old value: tell the user to run `/kit:adopt --update`
  so the header and `W8` / `M9` name the brand file.
- If `impeccable` is installed and `.impeccable.md` does not exist, create it with only:
  `## Design Context` and the line "Source of truth: docs/brand.md (Design context, Tokens,
  Typography, Voice and tone). Read it before any design work."

## 9. Hand over

Report: the files written; the direction chosen and why; the contrast table; the method
skills used and the ones missing; open questions (logo, font licenses). Next step: a builder
task that mirrors the tokens into the theme (web: `@theme` in the global CSS plus the HeroUI
variable mapping; mobile: the theme module), committed together with `docs/brand.md`. From
then on `kit:auditor-ux` checks colors, typography and voice against the doc.

# /kit:audit

You orchestrate read-only auditors and merge their reports. You never fix code here, never
commit, and never edit a project file except the kit's own state files
(`.claude/kit-audit-state.json`, `.claude/kit-seal.json`).

**Paths.** The kit plugin root is `../../` from THIS skill's folder:
`<kit>/scripts/arch-check.mjs` and `<kit>/scripts/seal-write.mjs` (use absolute paths in
commands).

## 1. Parse the request

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| (none) | the chain of the project's rigor |
| `quick` | architecture only: `arch-check.mjs`, no agent (add `--explain` to have `kit:auditor-rules` explain the findings) |
| `full` | the whole `audit.chain`, whatever the rigor |
| `--milestone` | add `audit.milestone` (`judgment`, `senior`) |
| `--only a,b` | run only these auditors (used by `/kit:phase-done` to re-run what failed) |
| `--all` | the whole repository instead of the change (census) |
| `paths…` | audit exactly these paths |

## 2. Read the configuration

Read `.claude/kit.json`: `rigor` (default `standard`), scopes (`name → kind, stack, path,
mode`), `audit.chain`, `audit.milestone`, `seal`. Missing → tell the user to run
`/kit:adopt`; `quick` still works (general checks only); otherwise use the chain
`rules, tests`.

## 3. Resolve the paths and scopes

Paths from the arguments, or the change:

```bash
git diff HEAD --name-status
git ls-files --others --exclude-standard
```

- Map each path to the scope with the longest matching `path`; drop paths of `off`
  scopes; keep the rest (files outside every scope are "shared").
- Keep deleted files in the list for the seal; auditors skip them.
- Nothing left → print "Nothing to audit (no changes in enforced or reported scopes)" and
  stop. Do not write a seal.
- When several sessions share the tree, audit only the paths of THIS task: if `git status`
  shows files you did not touch, ask the user which belong to the task (or use the paths
  the builder report lists).

## 4. Choose the auditors

1. **Always first: the architecture pass** (zero tokens):

   ```bash
   node "<kit>/scripts/arch-check.mjs" [--all] -- <paths>; echo "exit=$?"
   ```

   Exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 could not run (show the error, continue with the agents).
2. **Mode → chain**:
   - `quick`, or no mode with `rigor: lite` → the architecture pass is the whole audit.
   - no mode with `rigor: standard` → `rules`, `tests`.
   - no mode with `rigor: full`, or `full` → every auditor of `audit.chain`.
   - `--milestone` → add `audit.milestone`. `--only` → exactly that list.
3. **Drop what has nothing to look at** (say so in the merged report):
   - `ux` when no UI file changed (no `.tsx .jsx .astro .vue .css` or locale file in a
     `web`/`mobile` scope);
   - `security` when the change is only docs, tests or styles;
   - `challenge` when no task or requirement ID is known for the change and `--all` was not
     given (ask the user for the task ID instead of guessing);
   - docs-only change → only `rules`.

## 4b. External skills for each auditor

The kit bundles no third-party skills; `../kickoff/external-skills.json` lists the ones
that sharpen an audit (`{ skills: [{ name, purpose, useWhen: { kind, stack }, source,
install, update, checkPath, license, usedBy }] }`). For each auditor you will launch:

1. Take the entries whose `usedBy` names that auditor (`auditor-ux`, or `kit:auditor-ux`)
   and whose `useWhen` matches a touched scope (`kind`/`stack` may be a string, a list or
   `*`; a missing field matches anything).
2. Expand `checkPath` (`~` = the home folder) and test it (`ls -d <path>`).
3. Pass the result in that auditor's prompt (step 5): installed → the path of the skill's
   `SKILL.md`; missing → its `install` command.

No file (older kit) → pass "none" and go on. A missing skill never stops the audit; it is
one owner note.

## 5. Tell the user the cost, then run

Before launching agents, print one line, e.g.:
"Running 3 auditors in parallel (rules, tests, security). Each reads the change on its own,
so this costs about 3× the tokens of one audit. Say 'sequential' next time to run them one
by one."

Launch every chosen auditor in ONE message (parallel) with the Agent tool,
`subagent_type: "kit:auditor-<name>"` — sequentially only if the user asked. Prompt for each:

```
Audit this change. Mode: <default|full|milestone>. Rigor: <rigor>.
Paths (audit ONLY these): <list>
Scopes touched: <name (kind, stack, path, mode)> …
Task / requirement IDs: <ids or "unknown">
Base: HEAD (working tree + index + untracked) | <range for milestones>
Architecture pass (arch-check) report:            ← for auditor-rules only
<the full arch-check output>
External skills for you: <name: installed at <path>/SKILL.md | missing, install: <command>> … | none
Kit scripts folder: <kit>/scripts
Return ONLY your report in the kit format (## title, ### Passed, ### Findings,
### Pre-existing (not counted), ### Notes for the owner, VERDICT line).
```

## 6. Merge into one report

From each report take the `VERDICT` line, the Findings rows, the Pre-existing rows and the
notes. `auditor-senior` is advisory: its points go to a separate "Advisory" section and
never change the verdict.

```markdown
## /kit:audit — <mode> · rigor <rigor> · <n> files · <scopes>
| Auditor | Verdict |
|---|---|
| arch-check | PASS |
| rules | FAIL (0 BLOCKER, 2 HIGH) |
| tests | PASS |
### Findings
| Auditor | Sev | Rule | File:line | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
### Pre-existing (not counted)
| Auditor | Sev | Rule | File:line | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
### Notes for the owner
- <deduplicated notes: deploy order, env to load by hand, OTA vs native build, manual checks>
### Advisory (auditor-senior)
<if it ran>
VERDICT: PASS | FAIL (<total> BLOCKER, <total> HIGH)
```

- Sort findings BLOCKER → HIGH → MEDIUM → LOW; merge duplicates (same file:line and rule)
  keeping every auditor name.
- Overall `FAIL` iff any auditor (arch-check included) counted a BLOCKER or HIGH.
- Skipped auditors are listed with the reason ("ux: no UI files").

## 7. Record the state

Write `.claude/kit-audit-state.json` (git-ignored) so `/kit:phase-done` can re-run only
what failed:

```json
{ "at": "<ISO time>", "mode": "default", "rigor": "standard", "paths": ["…"],
  "results": { "arch-check": "PASS", "rules": "FAIL (0 BLOCKER, 2 HIGH)", "tests": "PASS" },
  "verdict": "FAIL" }
```

## 8. Seal (only with `"seal": true`)

On an overall PASS, seal exactly the audited files (files, not folders; deleted files
included):

```bash
node "<kit>/scripts/seal-write.mjs" -- <path> <path> …; echo "exit=$?"
```

On FAIL, write nothing: the commit hook keeps blocking until a PASS. Remind the user that
any edit after the seal invalidates it for that file.

## 9. What next

- FAIL → hand the findings to the builder of that scope; after the fixes run
  `/kit:phase-done` (it re-runs only the failed auditors) or `/kit:audit --only <failed>`.
- PASS → `/kit:phase-done` to tick the progress log and draft the commit message.
- `quick` found BLOCKERs in secrets → tell the user to rotate the key now, before anything
  else.

## What to build (all money in BigInt cents — P1; JSON amounts are digit strings)
Prisma 7 (`prisma.config.ts`, driver adapter `@prisma/adapter-pg`, migrations by `prisma migrate diff` — AN8, never `migrate dev`). Models (snake_case tables, `Timestamptz(3)`, explicit onDelete, indexes): users (email unique, password_hash argon2id, full_name, role), refresh_tokens (hashed, family id, expires_at, revoked_at), accounts (customer_id, status enum PENDING_COLLATERAL|ACTIVE|FROZEN|CLOSED, collateral_cents, credit_limit_cents, held_cents, posted_debt_cents, card_last4, card_token unique, card_expires, opened/activated/closed_at; CHECKs: all ≥ 0 and `held + posted_debt <= credit_limit` for ACTIVE/FROZEN; partial unique index: one non-CLOSED account per customer), collateral_deposits (amount, status PENDING|CONFIRMED|FAILED, limit_ratio_bps stored at request time — MO5, provider_payment_id, approve_url), repayments (same shape), payouts (account_id, amount, status, provider_payment_id), authorizations (account_id nullable, card_token_hint, amount, captured, status APPROVED|DECLINED|CAPTURED|REVERSED, decline_reason, merchant_name, merchant_mcc), journal_entries (kind, account_id, description, created_at) + postings (entry_id, ledger_account, amount signed BIGINT) with a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint trigger that rejects an entry whose postings do not sum to 0 (hand-written SQL in the migration, documented with `///`), idempotency_keys (scope, key, request_hash, status, response_status, response_body jsonb, unique(scope,key)), audit_log (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, request_id, data jsonb), outbox_events (type, payload jsonb, available_at, attempts, processed_at, last_error).
Ledger accounts: `collateral:{accountId}` (liability), `receivable:{accountId}` (asset), `cash_clearing`, `merchant_settlement`. Entries: deposit confirmed DR cash_clearing / CR collateral; capture DR receivable / CR merchant_settlement; repayment confirmed DR cash_clearing / CR receivable; close: apply min(debt, collateral) DR collateral / CR receivable, release the rest DR collateral / CR cash_clearing (payout).
Core helpers (src/core): money (BigInt ops), `runInTransaction` with ONE retry helper for 40001/40P01 (3 tries with jitter, then 409 `operation.in_progress`) and `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '3s'`; account lock = `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` as the first statement (ADR-0003); idempotency helper (ADR-0004): required `Idempotency-Key` header (UUID; missing → 422 `idempotency.key_required`) on every money POST, request hash = sha256(route + canonical body), same key+same hash completed → replay stored response, pending → 409 `idempotency.in_progress`, different hash → 409 `idempotency.key_reused`, the response saved in the SAME transaction as the effect; audit log row + outbox row written in the same transaction as each state change; payment provider client behind a port (A9) with `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`, signed with PROVIDER_API_SECRET (outgoing calls to card-network's provider API use `signRequest` with that secret).
Endpoints (prefix `/v1`; responses = contract schemas; errors = catalog codes):
- Auth (A12: stricter `@Throttle()` on these): `POST /auth/register` (customer, returns Session), `POST /auth/login` {email,password,audience} (role must equal audience else `auth.invalid_credentials`; constant-time-ish: always run argon2.verify), `POST /auth/refresh` (refresh token from httpOnly cookie `acme_rt`, SameSite=Strict, Path=/v1/auth, Secure from env COOKIE_SECURE; rotation; reuse of a revoked token revokes the family → 401 `auth.session_expired`), `POST /auth/logout` (204, revokes). Access token: JWT HS256 (jose), 15 min, claims sub + role. `GET /me`.
- Customer (`@Roles('customer')`, ownership enforced — another customer's account → 404 `common.not_found`): `POST /accounts` (idempotent; one open account → 409 `account.already_open`); `GET /accounts/me` (404 if none); `POST /accounts/:id/deposits` {amountCents} (MIN/MAX_DEPOSIT_CENTS from contracts → 422 `deposit.amount_out_of_range`; allowed while PENDING_COLLATERAL or ACTIVE — a deposit on an ACTIVE account raises the limit, R-55; creates provider payment with reference=deposit id, returns Deposit with checkout {paymentId, approveUrl}); `GET /accounts/:id/deposits`; `POST /accounts/:id/repayments` {amountCents} (≤ postedDebt else 422 `repayment.exceeds_debt`; no debt → 409 `repayment.no_debt`); `GET /accounts/:id/repayments`; `GET /accounts/:id/activity` (cursor page of Activity, newest first); `GET /accounts/:id/authorizations` (page); `POST /accounts/:id/freeze` / `unfreeze` (idempotent; codes `account.not_active` / `account.not_frozen`); `POST /accounts/:id/close` (idempotent; pending holds → 409 `account.pending_holds`; returns CloseAccountResponse with settlement; creates a payout row + outbox event `payout.requested` for the released amount).
- Card network (`@Signed('network')`, idempotent): `POST /network/authorizations` (resolve card token → account; decide INSIDE the locked transaction: unknown token → DECLINED invalid_card (accountId null); FROZEN → card_frozen; not ACTIVE → account_not_active; amount > available → insufficient_funds; else APPROVED and held += amount via conditional update with row-count check — MO3; declined attempts are stored too; returns Authorization, HTTP 201 for both), `POST /network/authorizations/:id/capture` {amountCents} (only APPROVED → else 409 `authorization.not_capturable`; amount ≤ authorized → else 422 `authorization.capture_exceeds_hold`; held -= authorized, posted_debt += captured, journal entry), `POST /network/authorizations/:id/reversal` (only APPROVED → else 409 `authorization.not_reversible`; release hold).
- Provider webhook (`@Signed('provider')`): `POST /webhooks/payments` {paymentId, reference} → 204. Re-read the payment at the provider by id (MO4), verify reference + amount + purpose match OUR row; SUCCEEDED → confirm (deposit: collateral += amount, limit += amount × ratio_bps/10000, PENDING_COLLATERAL → ACTIVE and issue the card: last4 random, token `card_` + 24 random base64url chars, expiry 4 years; repayment: posted_debt -= min(amount, debt)); FAILED → mark FAILED; already settled → no-op (idempotent). Unknown reference → 404. Provider 5xx/timeout → no state change, 503 `payment.provider_unavailable` (the provider retries).
- Admin (`@Roles('admin')`): `GET /admin/dashboard` (Dashboard incl. ledger trial balance = SUM(postings) must be "0"), `GET /admin/accounts` (page, filters status/q on email/name), `GET /admin/accounts/:id` (AdminAccount), `GET /admin/accounts/:id/ledger` (JournalEntry page), `GET /admin/accounts/:id/authorizations`, `GET /admin/ledger` (all entries page), `GET /admin/audit-log?entityId=`, `POST /admin/accounts/:id/freeze|unfreeze|close` (idempotent, audit actor admin).
- `GET /ready` (@Public, DB ping) next to /health.
- Worker: `src/worker.ts` + `worker.module.ts` (separate entrypoint, P2): claims outbox rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, handles `payout.requested` (create provider payout payment, purpose payout; on success mark payout SENT) and a sweep that re-asks the provider about deposits/repayments PENDING for > 60 s and settles them through the SAME confirm path (MO4). Capped attempts with backoff; last failure logged. Add `start:worker` script.
- Seed (`prisma/seed.ts`): admin from env SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL / SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD and a demo customer SEED_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / SEED_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD (idempotent upserts). Add scripts `db:migrate` (`prisma migrate deploy`), `db:seed`.
- Env schema (extend `baseEnvSchema(3000)` in src/core/config/env.ts): DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET (min 32), ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS (900), REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS (604800), COOKIE_SECURE (bool, default false), NETWORK_SIGNING_SECRET, PROVIDER_SIGNING_SECRET (webhooks from the provider), PROVIDER_API_URL (card-network base, e.g. http://localhost:3001), PROVIDER_API_SECRET (our calls to the provider), SEED_* vars. Production fails closed.
- Dockerfile: the api container must run migrations + seed on start (e.g. a `start:prod` script `prisma migrate deploy && node dist/prisma/seed.js && node dist/main.js` or similar) — make sure `pnpm deploy --prod` output contains what it needs (prisma CLI is a devDependency today: if migrations need it at runtime, move what's needed and tell me; do not edit infra/). Also the generated Prisma client location must be inside the deploy output.

## What it simulates
The lending core (apps/api, port 3000) is the system of record. This service plays two external parties (ADR-0001), state kept IN MEMORY (it is a simulator; document that a restart forgets payments):

### 1. Card network / merchant acquirer
- `POST /v1/purchases` (`@Public()` — the card token is the credential; stricter `@Throttle()`): body = `purchaseRequestSchema` (cardToken, amountCents, merchant {name, mcc}); header `Idempotency-Key` (UUID) REQUIRED from the browser (missing → 422 `idempotency.key_required`); the same key with the same body returns the same stored result (in-memory map), with a different body → 409 `idempotency.key_reused`. It forwards to the core `POST {CORE_API_URL}/v1/network/authorizations` with body `networkAuthorizationRequestSchema`, header `Idempotency-Key` = the browser's key, signed with `signRequest({secret: NETWORK_SIGNING_SECRET, method, path: '/v1/network/authorizations', rawBody})` (the path signed is the request path incl. `/v1`), `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`; on timeout / network error / 5xx retry up to 3 times with backoff and the SAME key (the core is idempotent); a 4xx is final. Map the core's Authorization to `purchaseResultSchema` (availableCents: null unless the core returns it — it does not; keep null). If the core is unreachable after retries → 503 `payment.provider_unavailable`.
- After an APPROVED purchase, schedule a capture after `CAPTURE_DELAY_MS` (default 4000): `POST /v1/network/authorizations/:id/capture` {amountCents = authorized amount}, signed, `Idempotency-Key` = deterministic UUID v5-like derived from the authorization id (or store a generated one per authorization), retried with backoff on failure (max 5). Keep a small in-memory scheduler that is cleaned up on app shutdown (`enableShutdownHooks` is on).
- `POST /v1/purchases/:authorizationId/void` (`@Public()`, Idempotency-Key required): if the capture has not happened yet, cancel the scheduled capture and call the core's `POST /v1/network/authorizations/:id/reversal` (signed, idempotent); otherwise 409 `authorization.not_reversible`.
- CORS: the customer web app calls `/v1/purchases` from the browser (origins from env CORS_ORIGINS — nest-core handles it).

### 2. Payment provider ("Acme Bank" simulator)
- `POST /v1/provider/payments` (`@Signed('core')`, secret PROVIDER_API_SECRET): body `providerCreatePaymentSchema` {reference, amountCents, purpose}; idempotent by `reference` (same reference → same payment); returns `providerPaymentSchema` with `approveUrl = {PUBLIC_URL}/provider/pay/{id}`. Purpose `payout` → succeeds immediately (status SUCCEEDED) and a webhook is sent.
- `GET /v1/provider/payments/:id` (`@Signed('core')`) → `providerPaymentSchema` (404 unknown). This is what the core re-reads (MO4).
- `GET /provider/pay/:id` (`@Public()`): a small server-rendered HTML page (no JS needed): "Acme Bank (simulator)", the amount formatted with `formatCents` from contracts, the purpose ("Security deposit to Acme Credit" / "Card payment to Acme Credit"), and two buttons in `<form method="post">`: Approve / Decline. Unknown id → a 404 page. Already settled → show the final status. Keep it accessible (labels, lang="en", contrast) and CSP-safe (helmet is on: no inline scripts; inline `<style>` is blocked by helmet's default CSP — serve a tiny stylesheet from a route or use no styling beyond semantic HTML + a linked CSS route). Copy is English. A "Return to Acme Credit" link goes to `{WEB_URL}/app` (env).
- `POST /provider/pay/:id/approve` and `/decline` (`@Public()`, form posts — HTML form encoding: add `app.useBodyParser('urlencoded', …)` ONLY if needed and only via your app module/bootstrap without editing nest-core; alternatively make the buttons plain POSTs with no body): set SUCCEEDED / FAILED (only from PENDING; idempotent), then send the webhook `POST {CORE_API_URL}/v1/webhooks/payments` {paymentId, reference} signed with `signRequest({secret: PROVIDER_SIGNING_SECRET, …})`, retried with backoff (max 5) until the core answers 2xx or a final 4xx; then redirect (303) back to the pay page showing the result.
- A webhook is also re-sent by `POST /v1/provider/payments/:id/resend-webhook` (`@Signed('core')`) — optional; skip if time is short.

## API (core, prefix /v1; JSON; errors = `{code, message, details?, requestId}`)
Auth: `POST /auth/register` {email,password,fullName} → Session; `POST /auth/login` {email,password,audience:'customer'} → Session {accessToken, expiresInSeconds, user} + sets httpOnly refresh cookie (send `credentials: 'include'`); `POST /auth/refresh` (cookie) → Session; `POST /auth/logout` → 204; `GET /me`.
Access token in MEMORY only (Zustand store without persist); on load the session gate calls /auth/refresh once (single-flight), redirects to /signin without a session. Every API call: `Authorization: Bearer`, `credentials: 'include'`, on 401 try one refresh then retry once.
Customer: `POST /accounts` (Idempotency-Key) → Account; `GET /accounts/me` → Account (404 = no account yet); `POST /accounts/:id/deposits` {amountCents} (Idempotency-Key) → Deposit {status PENDING, checkout {paymentId, approveUrl}}; `GET /accounts/:id/deposits`; `POST /accounts/:id/repayments` {amountCents} (Idempotency-Key) → Repayment with checkout; `GET /accounts/:id/repayments`; `GET /accounts/:id/activity?cursor&limit` → {items: Activity[], nextCursor}; `GET /accounts/:id/authorizations` (page); `POST /accounts/:id/freeze` | `/unfreeze` (Idempotency-Key) → Account; `POST /accounts/:id/close` (Idempotency-Key) → {account, settlement {collateralCents, appliedToDebtCents, releasedCents}}.
Card network simulator (browser → port 3001, no auth header): `POST /v1/purchases` {cardToken, amountCents, merchant {name, mcc}} with Idempotency-Key → PurchaseResult {authorizationId, status APPROVED|DECLINED, declineReason}; `POST /v1/purchases/:authorizationId/void` (Idempotency-Key). Merchants list: `DEMO_MERCHANTS` in contracts.
Payment approval happens on the simulator's page at `checkout.approveUrl` (open in a new tab or same tab); after approving, the provider notifies the core; the app polls the account/deposit (TanStack refetchInterval with a stop condition — W3) until CONFIRMED/FAILED, max ~2 min.
Idempotency (MO2): every money POST carries a client-generated UUID key that survives reloads: persist per form intent in sessionStorage for 24 h (keyed by action + payload hash), reuse on retry, drop after a definitive answer. Disabled buttons are not idempotency.

## Screens (routes)
- `/` public landing (SEO-complete per WA6 now that it is public: unique title/description from i18n, canonical, OG/Twitter, JSON-LD (FinancialProduct or WebSite), one h1, `@astrojs/sitemap` is NOT installed — skip sitemap and say so; add `public/robots.txt`): hero explaining the secured card (deposit → limit → spend → repay → get the deposit back), CTA "Get started" → /signup, "Sign in". Astro-only (no island) except nav if needed. Remove the old placeholder `noindex`.
- `/signin`, `/signup`: forms (react-hook-form + zod schemas from contracts limits), error mapping by code (auth.invalid_credentials, auth.email_taken, common.rate_limited, generic), on success → /app.
- `/app` (authenticated, `client:only="react"` with an .astro skeleton fallback — WA2/WA11, noindex): the account home:
  - No account → onboarding card: explain + "Open my secured card" (POST /accounts).
  - PENDING_COLLATERAL → "Add security deposit" form (MoneyField, min $200 max $10,000 shown, parseMoneyInput, never type=number) → creates deposit → shows "Approve the transfer at Acme Bank (simulator)" with a button to `approveUrl` and a waiting state with polling; FAILED → retry.
  - ACTIVE / FROZEN → card visual (brand-600 face, wordmark, brass stripe, •••• last4, expiry, FROZEN badge), balances with the ledger amount style: Available to spend (hero `text-balance`), Credit limit, On hold, Owed; the VaultMeter (collateral · used · available); actions: Simulate purchase, Make a payment, Add to deposit (raises limit), Freeze/Unfreeze, Close account.
  - CLOSED → settlement summary (deposit, applied to debt, returned to you) + "Open a new card".
- Simulate purchase (dialog or `/app/purchase`): pick a demo merchant, amount, submit to the network (Idempotency-Key) → result: Approved (show new available after refetch) or Declined with the reason in plain words (insufficient_funds: "This purchase of $X was declined: it's more than your available $Y. Make a payment or try a smaller amount."; card_frozen; account_not_active; invalid_card). Show recent purchases with status On hold → Posted (captured ~4 s later by the network; poll briefly) and a "Cancel" (void) while on hold.
- Make a payment: amount ≤ owed (validate client-side with the same rule; API returns repayment.exceeds_debt / repayment.no_debt) → approve at the bank → poll.
- Activity list (`/app/activity` or a section): infinite/cursor list of Activity with status chips (words + color), amounts in mono, tables become cards at 360 px.
- Close account: ConfirmDialog explaining what happens (debt paid from the deposit, the rest returned); pending holds → show `account.pending_holds` message.
- Sign out.
Every query: skeleton (isLoading), empty state with CTA, error state with retry (W13). Toasts only in mutations (sonner, one toaster per page). Errors by code with copy for every code the screen can receive (W6) + a generic fallback.

Models (snake_case tables, `Timestamptz(3)`, explicit onDelete, indexes): users (email unique, password_hash argon2id, full_name, role), refresh_tokens (hashed, family id, expires_at, revoked_at), accounts (customer_id, status enum PENDING_COLLATERAL|ACTIVE|FROZEN|CLOSED, collateral_cents, credit_limit_cents, held_cents, posted_debt_cents, card_last4, card_token unique, card_expires, opened/activated/closed_at; CHECKs: all ≥ 0 and `held + posted_debt <= credit_limit` while not CLOSED; partial unique index: one non-CLOSED account per customer), collateral_deposits (amount, status PENDING|CONFIRMED|FAILED, limit_ratio_bps stored at request time — MO5, provider_payment_id, approve_url), repayments (same shape), payouts (account_id, amount, status, provider_payment_id), authorizations (account_id nullable, amount, captured, status APPROVED|DECLINED|CAPTURED|REVERSED, decline_reason, merchant_name, merchant_mcc), journal_entries (kind, account_id, description) + postings (entry_id, ledger_account, amount signed BIGINT) with a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint trigger rejecting an entry whose postings do not sum to 0 (hand-written SQL in the migration, documented with `///`), idempotency_keys (scope, key, request_hash, status, response_status, response_body jsonb, unique(scope,key)), audit_log (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, request_id, data jsonb), outbox_events (type, payload jsonb, available_at, attempts, processed_at, last_error).
Ledger accounts: `collateral:{accountId}` (liability), `receivable:{accountId}` (asset), `cash_clearing`, `merchant_settlement`. Entries: deposit confirmed DR cash_clearing / CR collateral; capture DR receivable / CR merchant_settlement; repayment confirmed DR cash_clearing / CR receivable; close: apply min(debt, collateral) DR collateral / CR receivable, release the rest DR collateral / CR cash_clearing (payout).
Core helpers (src/core): money (BigInt ops), `runInTransaction` with ONE retry helper for 40001/40P01 (3 tries with jitter, then 409 `operation.in_progress`) and `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '3s'`; account lock = `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` as the first statement (ADR-0003); idempotency helper (ADR-0004): required `Idempotency-Key` header (UUID; missing → 422 `idempotency.key_required`) on every money POST, request hash = sha256(route + canonical body), same key+same hash completed → replay stored response, pending → 409 `idempotency.in_progress`, different hash → 409 `idempotency.key_reused`, response saved in the SAME transaction as the effect; audit log row + outbox row in the same transaction as each state change; payment provider client behind a port (A9) with `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`, signed with PROVIDER_API_SECRET via `signRequest` (the card-network service verifies it).
Provider API you call (implemented by the other builder in apps/card-network; contract in packages/contracts/src/provider.ts): `POST {PROVIDER_API_URL}/v1/provider/payments` {reference, amountCents, purpose} → ProviderPayment (with approveUrl; idempotent by reference; purpose payout succeeds at once); `GET {PROVIDER_API_URL}/v1/provider/payments/:id` → ProviderPayment. Both signed (path signed = the request path incl. `/v1`).
Endpoints (prefix `/v1`; responses = contract schemas; errors = catalog codes):
- Auth (stricter `@Throttle()`): `POST /auth/register` (customer → Session), `POST /auth/login` {email,password,audience} (role must equal audience else `auth.invalid_credentials`; always run argon2.verify), `POST /auth/refresh` (refresh token from httpOnly cookie `acme_rt`, SameSite=Strict, Path=/v1/auth, Secure from env COOKIE_SECURE; rotation; reuse of a revoked token revokes the family → 401 `auth.session_expired`), `POST /auth/logout` (204). Access token: JWT HS256 (jose), 15 min, claims sub + role. `GET /me` → userSchema.
- Customer (`@Roles('customer')`, ownership enforced — another customer's account → 404): `POST /accounts` (idempotent; one open account → 409 `account.already_open`); `GET /accounts/me` (404 if none); `POST /accounts/:id/deposits` {amountCents} (MIN/MAX_DEPOSIT_CENTS → 422 `deposit.amount_out_of_range`; allowed while PENDING_COLLATERAL or ACTIVE — on ACTIVE it raises the limit, R-55; creates provider payment reference=deposit id; returns Deposit with checkout); `GET /accounts/:id/deposits`; `POST /accounts/:id/repayments` {amountCents} (≤ postedDebt else 422 `repayment.exceeds_debt`; no debt → 409 `repayment.no_debt`); `GET /accounts/:id/repayments`; `GET /accounts/:id/activity` (cursor page of Activity, newest first); `GET /accounts/:id/authorizations` (page); `POST /accounts/:id/freeze` / `unfreeze` (idempotent; `account.not_active` / `account.not_frozen`); `POST /accounts/:id/close` (idempotent; pending holds → 409 `account.pending_holds`; returns CloseAccountResponse; creates a payout row + outbox event `payout.requested` for the released amount).
- Card network (`@Signed('network')`, idempotent): `POST /network/authorizations` (card token → account; decide INSIDE the locked transaction: unknown token → DECLINED invalid_card (accountId null); FROZEN → card_frozen; not ACTIVE → account_not_active; amount > available → insufficient_funds; else APPROVED and held += amount via conditional update with row-count check — MO3; declined attempts stored too; 201 for both), `POST /network/authorizations/:id/capture` {amountCents} (only APPROVED else 409 `authorization.not_capturable`; amount ≤ authorized else 422 `authorization.capture_exceeds_hold`; held -= authorized, posted_debt += captured, journal entry), `POST /network/authorizations/:id/reversal` (only APPROVED else 409 `authorization.not_reversible`; release the hold).
- Provider webhook (`@Signed('provider')`): `POST /webhooks/payments` {paymentId, reference} → 204. Re-read the payment at the provider (MO4), verify reference + amount + purpose against OUR row; SUCCEEDED → confirm (deposit: collateral += amount, limit += amount × ratio_bps/10000, PENDING_COLLATERAL → ACTIVE and issue the card: last4 random, token `card_` + 24 random base64url chars, expiry 4 years; repayment: posted_debt -= min(amount, debt)); FAILED → mark FAILED; already settled → no-op. Unknown reference → 404. Provider 5xx/timeout → no state change, 503 `payment.provider_unavailable`.
- Admin (`@Roles('admin')`): `GET /admin/dashboard` (Dashboard incl. trial balance = SUM(postings) = "0"), `GET /admin/accounts` (page, filters status / q on email or name), `GET /admin/accounts/:id` (AdminAccount), `GET /admin/accounts/:id/ledger`, `GET /admin/accounts/:id/authorizations`, `GET /admin/ledger`, `GET /admin/audit-log?entityId=`, `POST /admin/accounts/:id/freeze|unfreeze|close` (idempotent, audit actor admin).
- `GET /ready` (@Public, DB ping).
- Worker: `src/worker.ts` + `worker.module.ts` (separate entrypoint, P2): claims outbox rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, handles `payout.requested` (create provider payout payment; on success mark payout SENT) and a sweep that re-asks the provider about deposits/repayments PENDING > 60 s and settles them through the SAME confirm path (MO4). Capped attempts with backoff; last failure logged.
- Seed (`prisma/seed.ts`): admin SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL / SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD and a demo customer SEED_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / SEED_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD (idempotent upserts). Scripts `db:migrate`, `db:seed`, `start:prod`, `start:worker`.
- Env schema (extend `baseEnvSchema(3000)`): DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET (min 32), ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS (900), REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS (604800), COOKIE_SECURE (default false), NETWORK_SIGNING_SECRET, PROVIDER_SIGNING_SECRET, PROVIDER_API_URL, PROVIDER_API_SECRET, SEED_*. Production fails closed. Make sure `pnpm deploy --prod` output contains the generated Prisma client, prisma.config, schema and migrations.

`pnpm --filter @acme/api lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`, `test:integration` all exit 0. Report: files, every endpoint, env vars with local values for .env.example / compose, contract or nest-core changes, how to run the worker, test counts, anything left. Never commit.

</details>

>   - **Idempotency:** the stored response commits in the same transaction as the effect; replay / in-progress 409 / key-reused 409. Stable business errors are stored and replayed. If the provider fails after the deposit or repayment row exists, the key is parked RETRYABLE, so a retry with the same key resumes that row instead of creating a second one.
>   - **Audit + outbox:** `recordChange` writes both rows in the caller's transaction.
>   - **Provider adapter:** signed with `PROVIDER_API_SECRET`, `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`. A 4xx from the provider → `payment.not_confirmed`; 5xx, timeout or malformed answer → 503 `payment.provider_unavailable`.
>   - **Outbox relay:** claims with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` plus a 60 s lease, 8 attempts with backoff; the final failure is logged as an error.
>   
>   ### Worker
>   - **Run it:** `pnpm --filter @acme/api start:worker` (`node dist/worker.js`); for development, `dev:worker`.
>   - **Payouts:** handles `payout.requested` → provider payout by our payout id → marked SENT through the same settlement path as webhooks.
>   - **Sweep:** every 30 s, deposits and repayments still PENDING after 60 s are re-read at the provider and settled through that same path.
>   - **Container start (API):** `start:prod` = `node scripts/start-prod.mjs` (migrate deploy, then `dist/seed.js`, then `dist/main.js`). `package.json` has `files: [dist, prisma, prisma.config.ts, scripts]`, so `pnpm deploy --prod` ships the client, config, schema and migrations.
>   - Other scripts: `db:migrate`, `db:seed`, `db:diff`, `db:generate`.
>   
>   ### Env vars (for `.env.example` / compose)
>   | Var | Local value |
>   |---|---|
>   | `DATABASE_URL` | `postgresql://acme:«redacted»@localhost:5434/acme_credit` (compose: host `postgres:5432`) — required |
>   | `JWT_SECRET` | ≥ 32 chars |
>   | `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | 900 |
>   | `REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | 604800 |
>   | `COOKIE_SECURE` | false |
>   | `NETWORK_SIGNING_SECRET`, `PROVIDER_SIGNING_SECRET`, `PROVIDER_API_SECRET` | ≥ 32 chars, identical in card-network |
>   | `PROVIDER_API_URL` | default `http://localhost:3001`; compose `http://card-network:3001` |
>   | `SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | password ≥ 12 chars, seed only |
>   | `SEED_CUSTOMER_EMAIL` / `SEED_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD` | password ≥ 12 chars, seed only |
>   | `SHADOW_DATABASE_URL` | optional, only for `db:diff` |
>   
>   The four secrets default to `dev-only-…-not-a-real-secret` outside production — the same convention and strings as card-network. Production rejects those defaults.
>   
>   ### Tests
>   - **Integration** (`apps/api/test/integration/`; throwaway database per run, real migrations and real seed, real HTTP fake provider that checks signatures):
>     - `platform` — drift test, unbalanced entry rejected at commit, append-only journal, within-limit CHECK, outbox crash between claim and done (re-processed once).
>     - `lending` — open/replay/already_open, deposit boundary pairs 19999/20000 and 1000000/1000001, activation only after the provider confirms, limit taken from the stored ratio, forged webhook 401, unknown reference 404, tampered amount 409, provider down 503 with no state change, retry after outage resumes the same deposit, key reused 409, ownership 404 on reads and writes.
>     - `settlement` — repayments (no_debt, 5001 vs 5000, credit restored only after confirmation), freeze/unfreeze, pending holds 409, close releases or applies collateral, payout + outbox row, trial balance 0.
>     - `authorizations` — exactly available approved / +1 cent declined; **N=50 parallel → exactly 13 approved, held 19500, never over limit**; invalid / frozen / closed card declines; same-key replay keeps a single hold; partial capture and replay; reversal.
>     - `auth`, `admin`, `worker`, and `health` (route-marker scan: 0 violations).
>   - **Unit:** every money and business rule has boundary pairs (deposit range, repayment cap, available credit, capture ≤ hold, close settlement, ratio rounding, retry helper, idempotency states, token rotation).
>   
>   ### Deviations and open points
>   - **Seed location:** the seed is `src/seed.ts`, compiled to `dist/seed.js`, not `prisma/seed.ts`. This lets it reuse the env schema, `PrismaService` and the argon2 hasher. This deviates from the AN1 layout.
>   - **Repayment cap:** a new repayment may not exceed posted debt minus repayments still pending. Any excess confirmed after a close is refunded as a payout.
>   - **A deposit confirmed after the account closed** is posted, then immediately released and refunded as a payout.
>   - **Throttling:** I dropped the per-route deposit/repayment throttle (all integration traffic comes from one IP, and the simulated provider has no per-call cost); the global 120/min still applies. Network and webhook controllers use `@SkipThrottle()` because they are signed service traffic.
>   - **Not built:** R-53 monthly statements to object storage were not in this brief.

From the owner's main agent — two production-only bugs found in apps/web; avoid them in apps/admin:
1. Do NOT copy the manual `vite.build.rolldownOptions.output.codeSplitting` vendor groups from apps/web's astro.config — they broke hydration in the production build ("_ is not a function" in vendor-ui; islands never hydrate, and the sign-in form then submits natively as GET with the password in the URL). I removed them from apps/web. Use the default chunking (a chunk-size warning is acceptable for now).
2. Every `<form>` in an island must have `method="post"` (plus `noValidate`) so a failed hydration can never put credentials in a URL.
3. CSP: react-aria and sonner inject static `<style>` tags at runtime; I'm adding their sha256 hashes to `security.csp.styleDirective.hashes` in apps/web/astro.config.mjs — copy the same block into apps/admin's config when you see it there (I'll also do it at integration).
Verify hydration on a PRODUCTION build (`astro build` + `astro preview --port 4342`), not only `astro dev`: check `astro-island` elements lose their `ssr` attribute and the console has no CSP errors.

>   ## auditor-senior — milestone f0eb9ed..HEAD (F0–F8) (advisory)
>   
>   ### Top improvements (impact / effort)
>   
>   1. **Make approved holds expire in the core.**
>      - Why it matters: the card-network keeps pending captures in memory (`apps/card-network/src/modules/purchases/capture.service.ts:39`, "a restart forgets pending captures (the core keeps the holds)"). The core has no `EXPIRED` status (`AuthorizationStatus` enum in `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261021191651_lending_core/migration.sql`) and no TTL. Closing an account is refused while any hold exists (`apps/api/src/modules/accounts/helpers/account-rules.ts:62`, `account.pending_holds`).
>      - Consequence: if card-network restarts during the 4 s `CAPTURE_DELAY_MS` window, that hold never goes away. Available credit stays reduced for good, and the account can never close, so the collateral is never released. That breaks R-05. A fintech reviewer will ask "what happens to an auth that is never captured?" first.
>      - Change:
>        - Add `EXPIRED` and `expires_at` (authorization time + N days), indexed on `(status, expires_at)`.
>        - Add a `PeriodicJob` in `worker.module.ts` that releases holds under `lockAndRead`, with audit and outbox.
>        - A capture of an EXPIRED authorization answers `authorization.not_capturable`.
>        - Integration test with an injected clock.
>      - Effort: S–M. Impact: high.

>   - **Layout.**

>     - `api`: 2 tasks across AZs, `/health` ready check on the ALB target group, deregistration delay ≥ the 20 s transaction timeout.
>     - `worker`: 1–2 tasks. `SKIP LOCKED` makes N safe. Add a heartbeat metric so CloudWatch alarms when it stops.
>     - `card-network`: desired_count = 1, documented as a stateful simulator. In production this is an external party.
>     - `migrate`: a one-off task definition that CI runs before `update-service`. Remove migrate + seed from `start-prod.mjs` for AWS, and seed only in a demo env.
>   - **ALB.**
>     - HTTPS with ACM; customer/admin API on `api.<domain>`.
>     - Put `/v1/network/*` and `/v1/webhooks/*` behind their own listener rule with a WAF IP allowlist.
>     - WAF rate-based rules as the global limiter. Also set `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` in `nest-core/bootstrap.ts` (see Risks).

>   - **Rotate the demo passwords.** `admin@acme.test` / `ana@acme.test` use the passwords committed in `.env.example` (`Admi…`, `Cust…`) and baked into the bundles. >   - **Throttler behind a load balancer.** With no `trust proxy`, every user behind an ALB shares one IP: the 10/min login limit becomes global (a login denial-of-service), while a single attacker still gets 10 guesses per minute per real IP. ## 1. Fit the key content in the viewport on every device
TV (1920–2560 wide, ~1080 tall), desktop (1280–1440 × 800), iPad portrait/landscape (768×1024, 1024×768), phones (360×740, 390×844, 430×932). On phones the first screen must show the card-summary strip, available-to-spend and the primary actions above the floating tab bar; the rest may scroll. Use `h-dvh`/`min-h-0` grid layouts with `clamp()`-based spacing and type that scales with viewport height (allowed: brackets for `clamp()`/`dvh`), container max width that grows sensibly on TV (e.g. up to 1600px, centered, larger type) — no stretched empty areas, no clipped content, nothing hidden behind the floating tab bar. Apply the same "fits the viewport" discipline to Store (grid scrolls inside, cart summary always visible), Activity (list scrolls inside) and the new Card page.

## 2. Separate usage from card settings
- **Inicio / Home** (`/app`): only USAGE — available to spend (hero), credit limit, on hold, owed, the vault meter (backed by your security deposit), quick actions (Ir a la tienda primary, Hacer un pago, Agregar al depósito) and recent orders. A compact card summary (mini card thumbnail with •••• last4 + status chip) that links to the Card page is fine.
- **New page Tarjeta / Card** (`/app/card`, `/en/app/card`): the full card visual + card details (cardholder name from the session user, •••• last4, expiry, status Active/Frozen) + CARD SETTINGS: Freeze/Unfreeze as a switch-style control with explanation and confirmation (existing mutation, Idempotency-Key), "Agregar al depósito / Raise your limit" entry (existing deposit flow), "Copiar los últimos 4" or similar harmless detail action only if useful, and a link to Profile for closing the account. Make it look like a real, premium secured card in the brand: true card proportions (aspect-ratio 1.586/1, `aspect-[1.586]` is allowed as off-scale ratio), rounded 16px, ink outline + hard offset shadow; brand-yellow face (light and dark) with a subtle geometric pattern built from CSS only (e.g. layered radial/linear gradients using token colors — no images, no gradients-as-text, no purple-to-blue), an EMV chip drawn with CSS/inline icon component (lucide or a small SVG component in the icon wrapper folder — not inline <svg> in features), a contactless glyph, "Acme Credit" wordmark (Golos 700), a small "SECURED / GARANTIZADA" pill, cardholder name (uppercase, tracking), •••• last4 in mono large, "VENCE/EXPIRES 10/30", and a tiny network-style mark of our own (two overlapping circles in ink/violet — not a real network's logo). >   ### What changed and why
>   - **Keyset filter:** `olderThan` is now `field <= c AND (field < c OR id < cid)`. Same meaning as before, but I checked on a 200k-row table that Postgres can now start the index scan at the cursor; the old `OR` form can't bound the scan.
>   - **Cursor check:** `decodeCursor` only accepts the exact canonical ISO instant it writes. Before, `Date()` also accepted things like `2026-10-21` or offset forms.
>   - **Activity query:** each of the four sources applies the cursor, sorts and cuts to `limit+1` on its own, then the results are merged. Ids are compared as `uuid` in every branch. A page reads at most 4 × (limit+1) rows, however long the history.
>   - **Item counts:** these are now computed in TypeScript from the validated lines; the per-row `jsonb_array_elements` subquery is gone.
>   - **Parallel reads:** the ownership or existence check and the list query run in `Promise.all` (no transaction is involved). The cursor is decoded before either starts.
>     - Review bug, fixed test-first: in deposits, repayments and the admin ledger, a forged cursor threw while the check was already running, which would have left an unhandled rejection. The two tests failed first ("expected vi.fn() to not be called"), then passed.
>   - **Dashboard:** one CTE statement in `AdminRepository` replaces five sequential awaits.
>   - **Cache-Control:** set in the nest-core bootstrap, so the API and card-network both send `Cache-Control: private, no-store` on every response, including 4xx.

1. **Hold expiry + admin release.** Authorization holds that are never captured stay held forever, locking credit. Add `expiresAt` (policy e.g. 7 days, from config, recorded at authorization time — MO5) and a worker sweep that reverses expired APPROVED holds through the SAME reversal path (ledger + audit + outbox), idempotent, batched with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Concurrency test: capture ∥ release → exactly one wins.
2. **Payouts swept, retried, visible.** On close the collateral refund/payout is requested (payout.requested outbox) — make sure a payout that fails or times out at the provider is retried by a sweep with backoff and a capped attempt count, settled through one path, never paid twice (provider reference per attempt, MO5), its final failure reported (OB6/incident once), and expose `GET /v1/admin/payouts` (keyset-paginated like the other admin lists: `?limit&cursor&status`) + payout state on the admin account detail. Provider-down test: 5xx → no state change, retried later.
3. **PENDING repayments expire and do not block.** A repayment left PENDING (customer never approved at the bank) currently counts as "in flight" forever, blocking new repayments up to the debt. Add expiry (config, e.g. 30 min) — the sweep re-reads the provider first (MO4: uncertain ≠ no); only a provider-confirmed not-paid/expired payment is marked EXPIRED; a late approval still settles through the same path. Same for PENDING deposits if they share the code.
4. **Idempotency lease.** An IN_PROGRESS idempotency record whose request crashed blocks the key forever (409 operation.in_progress). Add a lease (`lockedUntil`, e.g. 60 s); after it expires a retry with the same key and payload may take over (atomic conditional update), never running the effect twice (the effect is in the same tx as the record, P1/MO2). Test: crashed record + expired lease → retry succeeds once; live lease → 409.
5. **frozenBy.** A customer can unfreeze a card the admin froze. Store `frozenBy` (CUSTOMER | ADMIN) and reason; customer unfreeze of an admin freeze → 409/403 with a catalog code (`account.frozen_by_admin`), admin can unfreeze both. Expose `frozenBy` in the customer and admin account responses (additive contract in packages/contracts) so the UI can explain it. Attacker test.
6. **Deposit cap per account (decision G11, proposal):** total confirmed + pending collateral per account ≤ USD 10,000.00 (the existing single-deposit max), one constant in packages/contracts shared with the UI (G12), checked under the account lock; over → 422 `payment.deposit_cap_exceeded` with details { maxCents, currentCents }. Boundary pair tests. Log it as `(proposal)` in the README Progress list per G11.
7. **Realistic seed fixtures** (dev/demo only, never in production unless SEED_DEMO_CUSTOMER=true — respect the guard already in env.ts/users.seeder): the demo customer gets an active account with a confirmed deposit, several captured store purchases with lines across the 4 merchants, one declined, one live hold, one repayment — created through the real services/ledger so balances reconcile (trial balance and cached balances match). Idempotent on re-run.

Add every new error code to the catalog + web/admin locale copy (es-MX and en-US) — only append keys (G14) in apps/web/src/app/i18n/locales/* and apps/admin/src/app/i18n/locales/*. Contract changes additive (A18), list them for the UI agent. Commands with exit codes: api lint/typecheck/test/test:integration/build, contracts test/typecheck, web+admin typecheck (fix only type breaks you cause). Mutation table (in-memory recipe, `--base vitest.config.mts --fsModuleCache=false`). Report files, migration name, contract diff, new codes, commands.

</details>

- **Fallaba porque Docker Desktop estaba cerrado.** Ahora `pnpm start` (o `pnpm docker:up`) primero comprueba Docker. Si está cerrado, abre Docker Desktop solo y espera hasta 3 minutos a que el motor responda. En Linux te dice que lo inicies a mano.

>   - **Hero.** It now fills one viewport (`--public-header-height` in `global.css`). Container is `max-w-7xl`, and the two CTAs sit side by side on phones. At 390×844 and 1440×900 the copy, CTAs and card are all above the fold. I didn't shoot 360×740 or 1280×800 after the final change.
>   - **Logo mark.** A mini Credi drawn as SVG with tokens only (`packages/ui/src/BrandMark.astro`). `Wordmark.astro` uses it, so it appears in the wallet, the landing and admin. The card face (`PaymentCard`) still shows the old square.
>   - **Favicons for both apps.** `node packages/ui/scripts/render-brand-assets.mjs` renders them with Playwright from `packages/ui/assets/brand/mark.svg`. It writes the SVG, 32/180/192/512 PNGs and `manifest.webmanifest` into both `public/` folders, plus `og.png` and `og-en.png` for web.
>   - **Admin files I touched:** `apps/admin/src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro` (4 icon/manifest `<link>` tags only) and the new files in `apps/admin/public/`.
>   - **Store cards.** Now compact, 4:3 image, name clamped to 2 lines, description 1 line from `sm`. Price and add button share one row, and "Agregar" collapses to "+" on cards under 16rem (container query). The grid auto-fills 10.5rem columns: 2 at 390, 1 at 360, about 3–4 at 1280/1440. >   ### What each item does
>   - **Splash:** about 1.6 s and never longer than 2 s. The mark pops and turns in, the letters slide up, Credi walks in and waves. Click or Esc skips it. It doesn't play on ClientRouter navigations; `?intro=1` replays it. Under reduced motion it shows the final frame and fades.
>   - **Walking mascot:** crosses about every 40 s, pauses on mouse hover, `aria-hidden`, hidden under reduced motion, and never takes taps on touch screens.
>   - **Tour:** 7 steps (wave → card strip → available → store tab → activity → card/freeze → celebrate). It has a spotlight, a floating card on desktop and a sheet on phones that moves to the top for tab-bar targets. Keys: ←/→/Esc, with Tab kept inside the dialog. Progress dots, "Saltar"/"Siguiente"/"Atrás". It's remembered in `localStorage` inside try/catch, and Perfil → "Ver tutorial" replays it via `/app?tour=1`.
>   - **Wallet rules:**
>     - When `frozenBy === 'ADMIN'` the card page says "Tu tarjeta fue congelada por Acme Credit" and hides the switch; a customer freeze keeps it.
>     - The deposit dialog shows the room left under `MAX_ACCOUNT_COLLATERAL_CENTS` and shows a notice instead of the form at the cap. The 422 shows its copy and keeps the typed amount.
>     - The EXPIRED payment label already existed.
>     - Order detail shows "Se libera sola" with `expiresAt` while on hold. The outcome and timeline now name the reversal reason (expired / admin_release / network).
>   - **Polish:** the hero balance overflowed at 390 px in es-MX ("USD 2,000.00"); I capped it at 11vw.

>   The kit's mutant recipe has a defect with Vitest 5. Its persistent `fsModuleCache` (repo `node_modules/.vitest-cache`) reuses the previous run's mutated transform, so mutants report "never applied" or the wrong verdict. These results come from runs with `--base vitest.config.mts --fsModuleCache=false`, after `vitest --clearCache`, and I cleared the cache again afterwards. The recipe's config should disable that cache; I didn't edit the kit files.

<details><summary>SendMessage — Tour trigger: every new sign-in (full instruction)</summary>

From the main agent — owner change for the wallet tour trigger: reviewers will share the same demo account, so "seen once" must not hide it from the next reviewer. New rule: the tour auto-starts after EVERY successful sign-in (the sign-in/sign-up success sets a one-shot flag, e.g. sessionStorage 'acme-tour-pending' = '1'; /app consumes it and starts the tour), NOT on reloads or ClientRouter navigations within the same login, and not on a session restored by refresh token. Keep "Saltar" and the Perfil "Ver tutorial" replay. Drop the permanent localStorage "done" gate (or keep it only as "don't auto-start again in this login"). Keep e2e working: e2e/support/intros.ts sets localStorage 'acme-tour-v1'='done' today — make the E2E bypass still work (e.g. honour a sessionStorage 'acme-tour-skip'='1' too, and tell me the key so I update intros.ts). Tests for: sign-in → tour starts; reload → no tour; sign out + sign in again → tour starts again.

</details>

<details><summary>SendMessage — Admin tour trigger: every new sign-in (full instruction)</summary>

From the main agent — owner change for the admin tour trigger: reviewers will share the same demo admin account, so "seen once on this device" must not hide it from the next reviewer. New rule: the tour auto-starts after EVERY successful admin sign-in (sign-in success sets a one-shot flag, e.g. sessionStorage 'acme-admin-tour-pending'='1'; the dashboard consumes it and starts the tour), NOT on reloads, ClientRouter navigations or a session restored by refresh token. Keep "Saltar" and "Ver el recorrido" replay; drop the permanent localStorage 'acme.admin.tour.seen' gate. Keep E2E working: e2e/support/intros.ts sets localStorage 'acme.admin.tour.seen'='1' today — honour a sessionStorage 'acme-admin-tour-skip'='1' bypass and tell me the key. Tests: sign-in → tour; reload → no tour; sign out + sign in → tour again.

</details>

**Claude:**

No lo hice por IP, sino algo que logra lo mismo de forma más confiable: **el tutorial arranca después de cada inicio de sesión**. Ya se lo pasé a los agentes de la wallet y del admin.

**Por qué no por IP:**
- **Hay que guardar IPs:** el backend tendría que registrar las IP de cada usuario, que son datos personales, solo para decidir si muestra un tutorial.
- **No es confiable:** detrás de una oficina o una VPN muchas personas comparten la misma IP. Y el evaluador que entre desde la misma red que tú no lo vería.
- **Ya no hace falta:** hoy el "ya lo vi" no está atado al usuario sino al navegador. Un evaluador que entre desde su compu lo ve aunque tú ya lo hayas visto con la misma cuenta demo.

**Cómo queda:**
- **Cada inicio de sesión:** al iniciar sesión, o al registrarse en la wallet, el tutorial arranca solo, aunque sea el mismo usuario y el mismo navegador.
- **Recargar o navegar** dentro de la misma sesión no lo vuelve a mostrar, para que no moleste.
- **Cerrar sesión y volver a entrar** lo muestra de nuevo.
- **"Saltar"** lo cierra, y **"Ver tutorial" / "Ver el recorrido"** lo repite cuando quieras.
- Los E2E siguen saltándolo con su propia marca, así que las pruebas no se rompen.

El auto-deploy y los rate limits quedaron listos y probados en local; falta subirlos. Hago el commit y el push cuando termine el agente de documentación de la API, porque compartimos un archivo. Ese push dispara el deploy automático en Render y ahí confirmo que el despliegue solo funciona.

**Auto-deploy:** con Render autorizado en todos tus repos, los servicios toman `erfajc97/acme-credit` con tus credenciales y tienen **Auto-Deploy: On Commit**.

**Rate limits contra DDoS y EDoS sin bloquear al revisor:**

| Capa | Qué hace |
|---|---|
| Borde de Render (Cloudflare) | Absorbe DDoS volumétrico. La wallet y el admin se sirven desde CDN, así que navegar no toca nuestros servidores |
| Cada ruta de la API | 3 ventanas por cliente: **50/s** (corta ráfagas), **300/min** y **6.000/h**. Una persona navegando hace unas pocas llamadas por página, muy por debajo |
| Quién es "el cliente" | **Usuario logueado: por su id. Anónimo: por IP.** Varios revisores detrás de la misma IP de oficina o VPN no se bloquean entre sí |
| Puertas caras | Login 10/min y 120/h; registro y apertura de cuenta 5/min y 60/h (crean filas permanentes); depósitos y pagos 10/min y 60/h por cliente; checkout 30/min; aprobación en el banco 10/min |
| Servidor a servidor | Las rutas firmadas con HMAC no tienen límite: una llamada sin firma se rechaza con 401 antes de hacer cualquier trabajo |
| Costo (EDoS) | Instancias de tamaño fijo, sin autoscaling: un ataque cuesta latencia, nunca una factura más grande. Además, cuerpos de hasta 1 MB y listas de máximo 10 filas |

Al probarlo encontré y corregí un bug mío: `@SkipThrottle()` sin argumentos solo salta la ventana "minuto". Las llamadas firmadas de card-network quedaban frenadas por la ventana de ráfaga, y 50 compras en paralelo daban 429. Ya hay un test que detecta ese bug.

**Verificado:**
- nest-core 24/24.
- API: integración 107/107.
- Card-network: integración en verde.
- Lint y typecheck en 0.

**Producción:** el worker tuvo errores de conexión a la base solo durante los primeros 4 segundos de arranque y desde entonces no registra fallos. La política quedó documentada en `docs/deploy.md` §11.

El agente de **documentación de la API** sigue trabajando: Swagger en `/docs` de la API y de card-network, y el diagrama de la base de datos en `docs/database.md`.

Para el navegador, la cookie que mantiene tu sesión era de terceros, y Safari y los navegadores móviles la bloquean. Mientras navegabas sin recargar todo funcionaba. - **Arreglo:** la cookie ahora es **particionada (CHIPS)**. El navegador la guarda aislada bajo el sitio de la wallet y la acepta. Verifiqué que el servidor emite `Partitioned; SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly`, con un test que falla sin el cambio.
